There are many benefits to pressure washing. It’s an excellent solution for dirty exterior surfaces, saving you time and effort. Whether you’re preparing to sell your house or just aiming to enhance its appearance, pressure washing can make a significant difference. Outsourcing the job to someone with experience will get you the best results. However, you might be curious about how much this will set you back cost-wise. The overall cost can vary depending on the scope of the project and the specific areas being power washed. Let’s dive into the various factors that influence the cost range of pressure washing. Pressure Washing vs. Power Washing While the terms “pressure washing” and “power washing” are often used interchangeably, there is a difference. The primary difference lies in the temperature of the water used—power washing uses hot water or steam, while pressure washing uses cold water. While hot water removes mold more effectively, power washing costs come with a slight increase. Because of this, it is recommended to opt for pressure washing unless you are dealing with deep stains. Average Pressure Washing Prices and Rates Breakdown As mentioned, there are various factors that influence the cost of pressure washing. Let’s explore these factors below: Per Hour Some companies charge for pressure washing on an hourly basis, typically ranging from $50 to $150 per hour. For context, most projects are completed within two to four hours, with the exterior of your home usually taking around two hours to power wash. Especially dirty areas or certain textured surfaces take longer to clean. Additionally, some companies enforce an hourly minimum charge, so even if the job takes only 30 minutes, you’ll still be billed for a full hour. Per Square Foot Many companies charge pressure washing by the square foot, typically between $0.30 to $0.80. Many pressure washing companies also charge minimums, typically anywhere between $100 and $350. Square feet can be calculated by multiplying the length of the surface by the width. Linear square feet, or the length of commonly power washed areas such as gutters or fences, typically are priced slightly higher. The more square feet a power washing service has to power wash, the cheaper per square foot the costs will be. On top of the square feet, you’ll also be charged about $2 an hour for the cost of water used. Many pressure washing companies will hook up to a water source local to your residence. Expect to see the job reflected on your next water bill. Opt for a different cleaning solution, as these areas should avoid being cleaned with chemicals. Gutters The average cost to pressure wash gutters is $200-400, depending on the linear feet of the gutters needing to be cleaned. Another factor is what story your gutters are located on. Taller homes require ladders and are more dangerous to clean, resulting in a higher charge. Dirty gutters stick out like a sore thumb after your house is freshly pressure washed. Fencing Pressure washing a fence ranges between $125-235, depending on the fence’s size. Pressure washing is a great option to renew a fence without having to spend thousands of dollars to replace it. Garage Floor The average cost to pressure wash a 300-square-foot garage floor is $100-200. Pressure washing your garage floor is a good idea before selling your home or if you’re treating your garage floor. Keep in mind any extra time that may be required to address grease stains. Windows The average cost to clean windows is $190-460. This is often a service homeowners choose to have completed at the same time as pressure washing. Dirty windows look even dirtier when next to clean siding. Cleaning windows is an additional charge; speak with your power washing service to see if this is something they provide. Commercial Building Vs. House Pressure Washing Pressure washing a home is cheaper than pressure washing a commercial building. Commercial buildings involve hard-to-reach spots, are often taller, and have more difficult roofs. For example, you’ll pay anywhere between $0.10 to $1.00 per square foot to pressure wash a commercial building, whereas you can expect to pay around $0.50 per square foot to pressure wash a home. DIY vs. Hiring a Tasker When it comes to deep cleans, there’s a lot to overlook. Regardless if you’re cleaning your outdoor furniture or garage, pressure washing is a very doable job. Keep in mind the cost of renting a pressure washer if you don’t own one as well as the cost of any additional tools (such as an extension hose), or the cost of purchasing a pressure washer yourself. Also keep in mind the damage that can happen if you don’t know what you’re doing, to either your siding, patio, or even lawn or garden. Get the average costs, pricing factors, and tips to get the best value for cleaning your home’s exterior surfaces. Pressure washing prices vary widely (as low as $75 and as high as $1,200) due to several factors. In this article, we explore the elements that influence the price for pressure washing and how you can get the best price for the service. Factors that influence pressure washing prices The area, surface type, and cleaning methods affect pressure washing costs. Here's a breakdown of each factor. Size and scope of the job The larger the surface, the more time, water, cleaning solution, energy, equipment, and labor it will take to complete the job. Pressure washing technicians typically calculate pricing based on the square footage and scope of the job. For instance, the average price to pressure wash a house is about $700. In comparison, the average price to pressure wash a driveway is $200. Type of surface being cleaned Different surfaces need varying levels of care, which results in various prices. Rugged, durable surfaces such as concrete, asphalt, or brick are easier to clean and can withstand higher water pressure. More delicate surfaces, such as wood decks or painted surfaces, require more caution and special equipment, increasing the time, cleaning solutions, and price. As such, concrete, asphalt, or gravel driveways range from $110 to $240, while wooden fences cost $120 to $300 to clean. Cleaning method and equipment used The cleaning method used also significantly influences the price. Power washing is more expensive because it uses a high-powered hot water machine. The specialized equipment and additional fuel costs for heating the water drive the cost up. On the other hand, pressure washing is less expensive because it uses cold water and doesn't require as much energy or specialized equipment. Soft washing is another cleaning method for delicate surfaces. It uses low-pressure water, specialized detergents, and equipment called a soft-washing pump. Although gentler, it is more expensive due to the additional chemicals and the need for more careful application to avoid damage. Location Pressure washing prices vary per region, depending on the local cost of living, service demand, and regional competition. For example, pressure washing services in Arizona can be as low as $75 in smaller towns. In contrast, New York sees a price range of $150 to $850, depending on the size and complexity of the job. Pressure washing price guide by job type How much does pressure washing cost per job type? Here's a breakdown of home pressure washing prices according to the job type, level of care, equipment, and cleaning solutions. House and siding Pressure washing a house’s siding costs between $250 and $1,200, depending on the size of the house and siding materials. Vinyl siding is generally the least expensive to clean, while brick and stucco cost more. Driveways and walkways Pressure washing a driveway or walkway costs between $100 and $300, depending on the size and material of the driveway, the amount of dirt and buildup, and the prep work required. Oil stains and deep cleaning can add $50 to $100 to the pressure wash price. Decks and patios The average price to pressure wash your decks and patios is between $100 and $400, depending on the material and size of the area. Sealing or staining after cleaning will add $100 to $300 to the pressure washing deck prices. Fences and outdoor structures Pressure washing fence prices are typically between $120 and $300, based on the material and size of the wall. The presence of old paint or stains can also affect the price. If the fence requires stripping or heavy prep work to remove peeling paint, the cost can increase to $400 or more. Roofs and gutters The average cost to pressure wash a roof is between $250 and $800, depending on the cleaning method used and the roof's size, pitch, and material. Likewise, gutter cleaning costs between $100 and $400, depending on the gutter's location, the house's size, and the amount of accumulated debris. Understanding pressure washing pricing models Pricing models are structured by square footage, by hour, or through flat-rate pricing. When requesting a pressure washing service, understand which model is used to avoid surprises. Pressure washing price per square foot Most pressure technicians charge per square foot, ranging from $0.10 to $0.80, depending on the surface type and the labor involved in cleaning. Prices for common surfaces like concrete driveways, sidewalks, and patios fall between $0.25 and $0.40 per square foot. More delicate surfaces, such as wooden decks, fences, or painted siding, cost a bit more, between $0.40 and $0.80 per square foot. One important consideration is that larger jobs reduce the cost per square foot. This is due to the economies of scale: larger areas are more efficient to clean because the crew can work more quickly and use equipment designed to handle bigger surfaces. Pressure washing prices per hour While pricing by square foot is typical, some pressure washing companies charge an hourly rate. This method is used where surface area isn’t easily measured or when the task involves more detailed work that doesn't fit into a square footage pricing model. Tasks like cleaning windows, gutters, or roofs fall under hourly rates. The condition of the surface impacts labor time. Surfaces with heavy dirt, grime, or stains require more cleaning time because the pressure washer needs multiple passes or additional cleaning solutions. Additionally, the area's accessibility significantly affects how long the cleaning will take. Areas that are difficult to reach, such as high walls, multi-story buildings, or tight spaces, require ladders or scaffolding to get these surfaces and take longer. Flat-rate pricing vs. custom quotes Sometimes, pressure washing companies offer flat rate pricing, especially for more standardized tasks that are easier to estimate in advance. You know what you'll be paying, and you don’t have to worry about additional costs unless there are significant changes in scope. However, custom quotes are more common for larger or multi-surface projects that require a more detailed assessment. With custom quotes, the pressure washing company will assess the area, the condition of the surfaces, and the job’s specific needs before providing an estimate. Request a detailed cost breakdown from multiple companies, including labor, equipment, cleaning solutions, and additional fees, and compare like-for-like services. This will ensure you're getting the best value for the service you need. Depending on the PSI, you can rent a pressure washer from $50 to $110 per day or buy one for anywhere between $300 and $6,000, depending on the model. You’ll also need to budget for cleaning solvents, ranging from $10 to $50. However, DIY pressure washing takes time, especially if you're inexperienced. What might take a professional only a few hours could take you an entire weekend, considering the time required for setup, execution, and clean-up. As a result, renting equipment for multiple days can add up and exceed the cost of hiring a professional. Additionally, DIY pressure washing comes with risks, such as damaging your home surfaces or injuring yourself. Professionals have the right tools, experience, and safety protocols to get the job done without the risk of damage or injury.
